understood: No goods tag for cattle exists yet, so I read the question as a word search across all manuscripts. It looks for the period words for cattle in the transcription, expanded text and translation: bue/buoi, vacca/vacche, giovenco, vitello/vitella, bestiame, bovino, and the Latin bos/boves and vacca. The results are grouped by page. Separate steps list the matching lines and entries so each hit can be checked, and isolate the street name Chiasso de' Buoi, which is not about animals.
limits: No goods are tagged as cattle, so this search runs on words only. It covers only the pages Conti includes today (51 of 593 MPAP 4 pages, plus a few in other manuscripts), and many of those are still uncorrected machine readings. A misspelled or heavily abbreviated word (for example b̄oi or vacħe) may be missed. 'Vitello' can mean veal rather than a live calf. 'Bestie' and soccida contracts may concern sheep, pigs or donkeys rather than cattle. Lines naming the Chiasso de' Buoi must be subtracted by hand using the 'street' step.

rows.translation: A farm with tenant's houses and a walled hut and an olive press, located in the parish of San Cristofano a Strada, in the place called a Bibbiano, bounded thus: on the 1st the road, on the 2nd the river Ema, on the 3rd Bindo di messer Jacopo de' Bardi, on the 4th Ruberto di Dosso de' Bardi They have let the said farm on lease for five years to Carlo di Giovanni da Macia [?], begin- ning on 1 August 1388. And he must pay ƒ thirty-two 𝒹 a year in rent. Instrument by the hand of ser Lapo Mazzei, notary of the officials of the Monte. And he must pay every six months in two payments, that is, half at each payment They have paid on 17 April 1389 ƒ nine 𝒹, to receipts of Simone at folio 9 They have paid on 26 June 1389 ƒ three 𝒹, to the said receipts at folio 9 They have paid on 14 August 1389 ƒa twelve 𝒹, to the said receipts at folio 6 They have paid on 13 December 1389 ƒ eight 𝒹 for [ƀƒ ?] of the rent, to the said receipts at folio 62 The said farm was sold by the officials of the Monte on 27 October 1389 to monna Agnola di Gherardozzo Bartoli for ƒ five hundred and fifty 𝒹. And the said 𝒹 were received by Bernardo Ardinghelli, treasurer of the said officials, from Gherardozzo Bartoli; of the said [sum] entered to receipts of Simone Fragli, agent, at folio 75 A farm with tenant's houses and a dovecote, with arable and vine-planted lands, located in the parish of San Martino a Sezzata, in the place called a Colombaia, bounded thus, that is: On the said farm there is a pair of oxen, which cost ƒa xxxiiiiº 𝒹; they are in sharecropping, half the profit and half the loss And there is on it a pair of pigs in sharecropping Filippo di Trullo and Fruosino called Chianti work the said farm together in sharecropping And the said Filippo had, on 26 June 1389, to add to [the price of] a pair of oxen, as appears in the outgoings of Simone Fragli, agent, at folio 18, ƒ vi ß xviii pc̄ He had on 15 June 1390 19 sheep and 4 goats in sharecropping, half the profit and half the loss; they cost ƒ twelve [paid to?] ser Agnolo the priest, to outgoings of Simone Fragli at folio 79, ƒ xii

answer.headline: Four MPAP 4 pages mention cattle: RS1139, RS1140, RS1141 and RS1147. Every one concerns pairs of plough oxen (buoi) on farms. No cows (vacche) appear in the pages searched.
answer.answer:
Searched only 65 of about 1,360 pages: the Finished or sent-to-training ones (51 MPAP 4, 12 UPenn 1435, 1 Baker MS 493, 1 UPenn 1321). Seventeen lines on 7 pages matched a word for cattle [pages, lines]. Only 4 of those pages are about animals. On RS1110 (4 lines) and RS1128 (1 line), "buoi" is part of the street name Chiasso de' Buoi, where houses are located or a debtor lives [street]. On Baker MS 493 img010, the 4 hits are the personal name "giovencho di giuliano", the man who brought payments in florins, not young bullocks [pages: ms493_img010, 4 rows].

The real cattle pages are all in MPAP 4, among the farm inventories of the heirs' estate, and all concern pairs of oxen ("uno paio di buoi") kept on poderi. The searches found no vacche, vitelli or general livestock words; the separate livestock search returned 0 lines [livestock]. RS1139 (1 line): the tenant of the podere at Strada must keep ƒ 16 for a pair of oxen on the farm. RS1147 (1 line): the same arrangement for Giuduccio[?] di Tuccio, lavoratore at Strada, ƒ sedici, July 388. RS1140 (2 lines): on the podere at Colombaia (Sezzata), a pair of oxen cost ƒa xxxiiiiº and was held a mezzo pro e mezzo danno. On 26 June 389 Filippo di Trullo had ƒ vi ß xviii pc̄ "ꝓ arogere a uno paio di buoi". RS1141 (4 lines): on the podere at Tramā (Sezzata), a pair valued at ƒ xxvi, one of which died in March 388. On 22 June 389 Francesco di Marco, called Chiocciola, had ƒ xi to buy back an ox ("ꝓricoꝓare uno bue"). A second podere on the same page, al Poggio, had a pair that cost ƒ xxxiii [lines; entries].

Counted by entry, 12 entries matched the cattle words, but only 5 of them (RS1139#1, RS1140#1, RS1141#1, RS1147#2) are really about oxen [entries]. All sums are as written, and none of them has been checked in the sums review (1 of 406 MPAP 4 sums checked). Dates are in Florentine style, as written.

caveats: Only 65 of about 1,360 pages were searched. Pages that are machine-read or still being corrected (about 540 MPAP 4 pages, including about 160 farm and house inventories) were not included, so the list is certainly incomplete.
The search matches words in the diplomatic text, so abbreviated or misread forms (e.g. b̄uoi, Kraken errors) can be missed. The TEI-expanded readings were not searched.
'giovencho' on Baker img010 is read here as a personal name from context ('recho giovencho di giuliano' = brought by Giovenco di Giuliano). This is an interpretation, not a tag.
RS1139/RS1147, and the ƒ 34 and ƒ 33 pairs on RS1140/RS1141, may describe the same animals or arrangements in different entries; they should not be added up as separate herds.
No sums here are checked. 'ƒa' on RS1140 is the open ƒa question in the MPAP 4 conventions.
followups: Run the same search once the TEI-imported MPAP 4 inventories are Finished, and include the TEI-expanded text (buoi, vacca, giovenco, bestie).
Check the oxen sums on RS1139, RS1140, RS1141 and RS1147 in the sums review, and confirm whether RS1139 and RS1147 record the same ƒ 16 obligation.
Tag Chiasso de' Buoi as a place and Giovenco di Giuliano as a person, so future cattle searches exclude them automatically.
